notes: Covers the 9.23 and 9.27 together. There are at least two generations under the 9.23 name.

gaps: It gives no treadmill part numbers and points to Precor's dealer site for those.
No chip part numbers are given.
method: Source: Precor service manual '9.23, 9.27 Treadmill' (Internet Archive copy of the Precor PDF; cover (c) 2004, PDF metadata last modified 2005), read as text on 2026-11-12; PDF page numbers match the printed ones.
Specs on p. 3: 2.75 hp continuous duty DC motor, 0.5-12 mph, 0-15% incline, 20 x 59 in. running surface, power 120 Vac 50/60 Hz at 15 A.
The manual wants a dedicated 15 A circuit (p. 27).
Every part claim here comes from this 9.23/9.27 manual.
An older Precor 9.23 service manual (manualzilla-id-7339463, cover (c) 2003, its software banner reads PRECOR M9.23) gives other specs (1.7 hp continuous duty, 51 x 17 in. surface, 0-10% incline).
Nothing from the older manual is used for parts.
Board-level parts named in the manual are the lower PCA (motor drive, incline relay drive, fuse, 12 Vdc supply) and a socketed PROM.
Qty 1 on extra parts is inferred from the manual describing one of each.

comps.spec: Drive motor 2.75 hp continuous duty DC, brushed (two brushes under snap-on covers, front and rear); motor and flywheel are balanced as a matched pair and replaced together; leads go to lower PCA terminals T3 (M+) and T4 (M-)

Lower PCA: PWM drive motor controller, current limit 28 A (drive shuts down if exceeded for 3-5 s); carries the fuse, 12 Vdc supply and incline relay drive; 7 LEDs (POWER, UP, DOWN, PWM, LIMIT, MOT DRV, SHUTDOWN); AC in on T1/T2, about 16 Vdc to the upper PCA on JK1

Incline up and incline down relays, driven from the lower PCA (its UP and DOWN LEDs show when each relay gets operating voltage); AC line voltage for the incline motor comes out on lower PCA connector JK4
Fuse on the lower PCA, replacement is a 3 A slow-blow; reads about 0.2 ohm when good
12 Vdc power supply on the lower PCA; its POWER LED shows the supply input is live
Treadmill circuit breaker with a reset button, wired with a separate on/off switch at the AC power cord entry; replaceable on its own

Incline (lift) motor, 0-15% grade, 120 Vac line voltage (105-120 Vac at lower PCA connector JK4) when the up or down relay is driven; one winding per direction; lift tube on a lift drive screw, length set at calibration; incline potentiometer under a cover on top
Incline position potentiometer, about 10 kohm end to end, three terminals, under a cover on top of the incline motor, read by the lower PCA on JK3; replaced with the incline motor
Speed sensor is a reed switch beside the drive roller pulley, closed once per revolution by a magnet in the pulley; connects to the lower PCA on JK2
Safety key: a magnet on the key operates a reed switch in the console
Drive belt from the drive motor pulley to the drive roller pulley, tensioned to about 80 lb (70-90 lb) by sliding the motor on slotted mounts; drive roller pulley carries the speed sensor magnet
Software PROM in a socket; the manual names two package styles in use, DIP28 and PLCC44
